newsitem.title: JAPAN: New US cabinet to keep Asia security ties--Mondale.
newsitem.headline: New US cabinet to keep Asia security ties--Mondale.

text.p: President Bill Clinton's new cabinet will not change U.S. security policy in the Asia-Pacific region, outgoing U.S. ambassador to Japan Walter Mondale said on Monday.
Mondale said the new cabinet members, including Samuel Berger, Clinton's national security adviser, would be key players in formulating security policy in Asia.
"Sandy Berger...has been one of the strongest supporters of our policy (in Asia)," Mondale, who leaves his post next Sunday, told reporters in his last news conference as ambassador.
"The national security adviser is very, very important - he sees the president every morning," he said.
Mondale said that new Secretary of State Madeleine Albright has close ties with Japanese officials.
Czech-born Albright was appointed on Thursday to succeed Warren Christopher in a sweeping shake-up by Clinton of his national security team.
Mondale also said that new Defence Secretary Senator William Cohen was "very familiar with security issues".
"I think this (new cabinet) is going to be a strong team," he added.
